pages.text: "Rain! Under the tree!" Big drops pattered into the yard. Yuki ran beneath the big tree. Brown dog Momo followed and shook all over.
"I'll play again when it stops. I'll wait here!" Yuki leaned against the trunk. The wide umbrella-like branches kept many drops away. Grandma called from the porch.
Flash! A little later, rumble, boom! Branches shook, showering water from the leaves. Yuki pressed palms over their ears.
"Not under the tree! Come here quickly!" Grandma waved from the porch. Yuki ran out through the rain, Momo beside them with ears flapping.
On the porch, Grandma dried Yuki with a towel. "Under a big tree is the most dangerous place in thunder. Inside the house is safest." Holding Yuki's hand, she said, "When Thunder Rumbles, Go Home!"
Inside the room, each flash lit the paper door. Thunder made it tremble. "The door must be startled!" Yuki held Grandma's sleeve.
Leaning on Grandma's lap, Yuki watched the brightening door. With Grandma beside them, nothing was scary. Yuki repeated, "When Thunder Rumbles, Go Home!"
The rain stopped, leaving the yard sparkling. From the porch's edge, Yuki saw a broken branch lying in the grass. Their eyes widened. "It could have been awful if I'd stayed there!"
Days later, thunder rumbled again. Yuki ran inside first. "One, leave the tree! Two, straight home! Three, stay inside until it stops!" Yuki fixed the scarf knot and shut the door.
Grandma sat Yuki on her lap and patted their back. Even in thunder, coming home made things all right. "Grandma, I'm not scared now! When Thunder Rumbles, Go Home!"
